title: BaseHarbor Console: product architecture and implementation plan
author: mcpdev80
body:
# BaseHarbor Console implementation plan

## Product definition

BaseHarbor Console is the complete visual operations surface for BaseHarbor: every BaseHarbor workflow plus deep runtime visibility, while BaseHarbor remains the single source of truth.

Hard rule:

```text
CLI / JSON / MCP / HTTP / Console
              ↓
       same BaseHarbor Core
```

## Core dependencies before v0.5

- mcpdev80/baseharbor#770 — shared Machine Operator Authorization
- mcpdev80/baseharbor#767 — protected HTTP machine API, execution identity, progress/events, logs and terminal streams
- mcpdev80/baseharbor#768 — provider-neutral Runtime Explorer, resource ownership and bounded runtime operations
- mcpdev80/baseharbor#769 — Runtime Provider != Target Access Provider

## Product areas

- Overview
- Applications
- Repositories
- Workspaces
- Targets
- Runtime Explorer
- Providers
- Observability
- Recovery
- Security
- Evidence
- Organization / Platform
- Settings

## Runtime model

Runtime resources are provider-neutral and may represent Docker/Podman resources now and Kubernetes/OpenShift resources later.

```text
Application
  -> Deployment
    -> Component / Provider
      -> Runtime realization
        -> Runtime resource
```

Ownership is authoritative, not guessed from names:

```text
managed | external | unmanaged | platform
```

## Target access

The Console never calls a Node Connector or runtime API directly.

```text
Console
  ↓
BaseHarbor HTTP
  ↓
Core / runtime semantics
  ↓
Target Access Provider
```

A future `baseharbor-node-connector` is an optional Target Access Provider implementation for remote hosts. Kubernetes/OpenShift normally use native APIs.

## Security

- shared BaseHarbor Machine Operator Authorization; no Console-local RBAC
- HTTPS only for Console/API/streams
- target-access transport security remains BaseHarbor #769
- no duplicate secret store
- no raw secret reveal by default
- safety class / policy / confirmation / ownership enforced server-side
- terminal/exec is explicit and auditable, never a hidden generic host shell

## Implementation phases

### Phase 0 — foundation now

- [x] new clean repository

### Phase 1 — read-only BaseHarbor

- Applications
- repositories / inspect
- workspaces
- targets
- providers
- status / doctor / evidence
- read-only Runtime Explorer
- operator session/authorization state

### Phase 2 — full BaseHarbor workflow parity

- graphical `app init` wizard using shared Core semantics
- workspace lifecycle
- target lifecycle
- plan/apply/update/repair
- provider lifecycle
- organization/policy
- backup/restore/destroy

### Phase 3 — runtime operations

- logs / live logs
- metrics
- inspect
- lifecycle operations
- images / volumes / networks
- container/pod terminal and exec
- managed/unmanaged reconciliation warnings

### Phase 4 — remote targets

Consume the Target Access Provider contract from BaseHarbor #769. The Console remains unaware of whether access is local, native API, optional node connector or a future cloud-native access implementation.

### Phase 5 — AI assistance

Explain / diagnose / plan / guarded actions through the same BaseHarbor machine operations. No generic shell and no secrets in AI context by default.

### Phase 6 — Kubernetes/OpenShift

Extend the same Runtime Explorer after BaseHarbor's Kubernetes/OpenShift runtime contracts exist. Do not build a separate OpenShift Console clone.

## Explicit non-goals

- no second orchestration engine
- no duplicate deployment state
- no Git hosting
- no browser IDE replacement
- no direct browser-to-Docker/Podman/Kubernetes APIs
- no Console-to-Node-Connector path
- no Console-local secret store
- no Console-local authorization model

## Source reuse from old prototype

Reuse selectively:

- Next.js/React/TypeScript approach
- Radix/Tailwind UI ideas
- Monaco
- xterm
- Recharts
- useful UX patterns for runtime views

Do not carry forward:

- old backend architecture
- direct Docker/Podman orchestration
- old local auth model
- old Agent architecture
- duplicate secret/control-plane state

## Acceptance

- every supported human-facing BaseHarbor operation has a Console representation
- repository -> inspect -> init -> plan -> apply works through the GUI
- runtime resources are visible from Application and Target context
- logs/terminal/metrics/events work through BaseHarbor streams
- managed/external/unmanaged/platform ownership is visible
- Console can evolve from Docker/Podman to Kubernetes/OpenShift without replacing its core architecture

## Normative UX / design rules

`docs/UX-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` is now the authoritative Console UX/UI specification.

All remaining implementation MUST follow it.

Key decisions:

- [x] grouped primary navigation: Overview / Develop / Operate / Observe / Protect / Platform
- [x] task-first and context-first page design
- [x] tables/structured lists as default for comparable operational resources
- [x] no card-wall dashboard pattern
- [x] detail pages use repeatable headers, context, actions and limited sibling tabs
- [x] complex app init/adoption uses an in-page wizard with final Review step
- [x] actions project BaseHarbor machine operations and SafetyClass
- [x] destructive actions use consequence-aware confirmation
- [x] status never relies on color alone
- [x] Overview prioritizes attention, target health, running operations and recent activity
- [x] desktop-first information density with responsive fallback
- [x] target WCAG 2.2 AA
- [x] Portainer excluded as a design reference

Next UI work should first refactor the existing shell, Overview, Application Detail and Runtime Detail against these normative rules before adding more large feature surfaces.

- [x] CA/client-certificate rotation
- [x] OpenBao recovery/setup flows where interactive
- [x] migration/replacement workflows with dependent choices

Shared requirements:

- [x] coherent decision cluster per step
- [x] visible progress/step state
- [x] smart defaults with provenance
- [x] detected/inherited/recommended/policy-required states distinguished
- [x] progressive disclosure
- [x] immediate + step + preflight validation
- [x] async discovery with retry and preserved state
- [x] safe Back/Cancel/Close semantics
- [x] resumable/draft-friendly architecture without browser-stored secrets
- [x] mandatory Review before complex mutation
- [x] semantic Plan/Diff where supported
- [x] SafetyClass-aware confirmations
- [x] explicit handling for dependency-invalidated choices
- [x] provider selection grouped by capability, not logo walls
- [x] semantic HA/availability choices before low-level replica topology
- [x] dedicated credential/certificate rotation UX
- [x] stronger restore preflight/review UX
- [x] actionable success state
- [x] recoverable failure state
- [x] WCAG 2.2 AA-oriented wizard accessibility

No complex BaseHarbor workflow should be implemented as an oversized modal or as a one-shot form when the task contains dependent decisions.

## Console deployment topology

Default topology:

```text
one BaseHarbor installation / security boundary
  -> one authoritative Core
  -> optional Console for that same installation
```

Typical shape:

```text
BaseHarbor installation
├── Core
├── PostgreSQL
├── OpenBao
├── managed Identity / Keycloak where enabled
└── Console
```

The Console is a client surface of the selected Core. It is not a global BaseHarbor authority and does not introduce a central Console backend that owns cross-installation state, authorization, routing or lifecycle.

Hard rules:

- Console state is presentation/client state only; Core remains authoritative.
- Console does not federate Dev/Test/Prod installations.
- Console does not proxy one BaseHarbor installation through another.
- Console does not create Baha-to-Baha communication or cross-installation reconciliation.
- Default browser deployment should use same-origin or a tightly bound trusted origin where practical.
- Authentication, authorization, policy, audit, deployment state, provider state and secret ownership remain with the selected installation/Core.
- Dev and Prod keep independent Console/Core/security boundaries when they are independent BaseHarbor installations.

Optional future multi-Core UX MAY exist as a client-side connection selector:

```text
Console client
├── Dev Core
├── Test Core
└── Prod Core
```

but selection connects directly to the chosen authorized Core. It MUST NOT become a central super-Core or shared authority.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Default Console deployment is documented as belonging to one BaseHarbor installation/Core/security boundary.
- [ ] Console live mode has exactly one selected authoritative Core at a time.
- [ ] No Console-local or central cross-installation deployment/authorization database exists.
- [ ] Same-origin/tightly bound trusted-origin browser deployment is the preferred default.
- [ ] Independent Dev/Prod installations remain independent when Console is enabled.
- [ ] Any future multi-Core selector is client-side only and preserves direct Core authority.
